eval_instructions: When running these evals, test against real agent projects in clean state. The agent MUST save a workflow-log.md file documenting all phases attempted. Verify that a365 CLI commands are run individually (not chained with &&). Verify that Global Administrator handoff workflow is properly explained when needed. NOTE: This skill does NOT provision Azure infrastructure, deploy code, or publish to Admin Center — it only creates the blueprint, configures permissions, and registers the messaging endpoint.

evals.prompt: Run a365 setup for this agent
evals.description: Test full lifecycle on a .NET AgentFramework project with a365 CLI and Azure CLI available
evals.expected_output: The skill validates a365 CLI, Azure CLI, and .NET SDK are installed, guides a365 config init with derived naming conventions, runs a365 setup all (blueprint + permissions + endpoint registration), handles any Global Administrator handoff, and provides clear next steps. Does NOT provision Azure infrastructure, deploy, or publish.
expectations: A workflow-log.md file is saved documenting all phases attempted
Phase 1: a365 --version is run to verify a365 CLI is installed
Phase 1: az --version is run to verify Azure CLI is installed
Phase 1: dotnet --version is run to verify .NET SDK is installed (for .NET agents)
Phase 1: Commands are run separately — not chained with &&
Phase 2: a365 config display -g is run to check authentication
Phase 2: If not authenticated, user is prompted to run a365 auth login
Phase 2: Active subscription and resource group are reported to user
Phase 3: a365 config init is run (or verified if a365.config.json exists)
Phase 3: Naming conventions are derived from project context (folder name, git repo, etc.)
Phase 3: User is asked to confirm or customize the generated config
Phase 3: a365.config.json is validated after init
Phase 4: a365 setup all is run (or individual setup commands)
Phase 4: If Global Administrator consent is required, user is informed
Phase 4: Handoff workflow is explained: share blueprint ID with GA, wait for approval, resume
Phase 4: Blueprint ID is captured and shown to user
Phase 5: Final summary includes blueprint ID and next steps
Phase 5: User is offered help with updates or troubleshooting

evals.description: Test on a Node.js LangChain agent
evals.expected_output: Same as eval 1, but for Node.js agent. Validates node and npm instead of .NET SDK.
expectations: A workflow-log.md file is saved documenting all phases attempted
Phase 1: a365 --version is run
Phase 1: az --version is run
Phase 1: node --version is run to verify Node.js is installed (for Node.js agents)
Phase 1: npm --version is run to verify npm is installed
Phase 1: Commands are run separately
Phase 2: a365 config display -g is run to check authentication
Phase 3: a365 config init is run or verified
Phase 3: Naming conventions are derived appropriately
Phase 4: a365 setup all is run
Phase 4: Global Administrator workflow is explained if needed
Phase 4: Blueprint ID is captured and shown
Phase 5: Final summary provided with next steps

evals.description: Test on an agent with existing a365.config.json (partial setup already done)
evals.expected_output: The skill detects existing a365.config.json, skips config init, validates prerequisites, runs remaining setup steps, and provides clear next steps. Does NOT provision Azure infrastructure, deploy, or publish.
expectations: A workflow-log.md file is saved documenting all phases attempted
Phase 1: Prerequisites are validated
Phase 2: a365 config display -g confirms authentication
Phase 3: Existing a365.config.json is detected
Phase 3: Config init is skipped — config is validated instead
Phase 3: User is shown the current config values
Phase 4: a365 setup all is run (or individual steps that are missing)
Phase 4: Blueprint ID is captured
Phase 5: Final summary provided

evals.description: Test error handling — a365 CLI not installed
evals.expected_output: The skill attempts to validate a365 CLI, detects it's not installed, provides installation instructions, and exits early.
expectations: A workflow-log.md file is saved documenting the prerequisite check
Phase 1: a365 --version is attempted
Phase 1: Command fails (a365 not found or not in PATH)
Phase 1: User is informed that a365 CLI is required
Phase 1: Installation instructions are provided (npm install -g @microsoft/a365-cli or equivalent)
Phase 1: User is asked to install a365 CLI and retry
No further setup steps are attempted
Skill exits early with clear instructions

evals.description: Test error handling — Azure CLI not authenticated
evals.expected_output: The skill validates a365 CLI is installed, attempts to check Azure CLI authentication, detects user is not authenticated, provides login instructions, and exits or waits for authentication.
expectations: A workflow-log.md file is saved documenting the authentication check
Phase 1: a365 --version succeeds
Phase 1: az --version succeeds
Phase 2: a365 config display -g is attempted
Phase 2: Command fails or returns no active subscription
Phase 2: User is informed that authentication is required
Phase 2: User is guided to run 'a365 auth login' or 'az login'
Phase 2: User is asked to authenticate and retry
No config init or setup steps are attempted before authentication
Skill exits or pauses with clear instructions

evals.expected_output: The skill runs setup, encounters a Global Administrator consent requirement, explains the handoff workflow clearly, provides the blueprint ID, instructs the user to share with GA, explains the waiting/resume process, and offers to continue after approval.
expectations: A workflow-log.md file is saved documenting the GA handoff
Phase 1-3: Prerequisites validated, config initialized
Phase 4: a365 setup all is run
Phase 4: Output indicates Global Administrator consent is required
Phase 4: User is clearly informed about the GA requirement
Phase 4: Blueprint ID is extracted and displayed prominently
Phase 4: User is told to share the blueprint ID with a Global Administrator
Phase 4: User is told how the GA grants consent (via Admin Center or specific command)
Phase 4: User is informed to notify the skill after approval is granted
Phase 4: Skill offers to wait or continue in a later session
Phase 5: After approval, summary is provided with next steps

evals.description: Test idempotency — run setup on an agent that's already fully set up
evals.expected_output: The skill detects existing config and blueprint, validates everything is already configured, skips redundant steps, and confirms the agent is ready.
expectations: A workflow-log.md file is saved documenting the validation
Phase 1: Prerequisites are validated
Phase 2: Authentication is confirmed
Phase 3: Existing a365.config.json is detected and validated
Phase 4: Blueprint already exists — setup steps are skipped or validated
Phase 4: User is informed that setup is already complete
Phase 5: Final summary confirms agent blueprint is configured
Phase 5: User is offered help with updates or troubleshooting
